main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling salted fish in the shared kitchen without smell affecting A's work, B's clothes and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B said the smell gets into clothes (T2) and later accepted the Tue/Thu after 7 and weekend plan (T18).

A-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T1, T3); A accepted D's schedule (T15) and C said it works (T19).

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1) and D said it's what he eats (T4); D then proposed cooking Tue/Thu after 7 or on weekends (T14) and A said it works (T15).

B-C.evidence: Both complained about smell on their things (T2, T3) and both accepted the final schedule (T18, T19), but they never addressed each other.

B-D.evidence: B complained about smell (T2) and suggested a door-shut fix (T6); D proposed the schedule (T14) and B said 'That's fine with me' (T18).

C-D.evidence: C said the laundry smells of fish and the yard is open (T3, T7); D offered not to cook when laundry is hanging (T8) and then proposed Tue/Thu/weekends (T14); C said 'Yes, that works for me' (T19).
